[Submission API](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/submission-api.html): Submission API documentation covering FINRA regulatory filing creation, validation, submission, updates, and retrieval, including Form U4, Form U5, Form BR, Create Individual, and Non-Registered Fingerprint workflows.

If you haven’t read [Getting Started](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/getting-started.html#getting-started), [Authentication and Client Creation](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/auth.html#auth) and [HTTP Client](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/client.html#client), please start by reading those sections.

The [Submission API](https://developer.finra.org/docs#submission_api) allows applications to create and update regulatory filings and other submission data to FINRA.

Each filing has a single method for submitting, validating and retrieving filing data. All endpoints require Firm credentials.

- [`Client.create_individual_submission()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.create_individual_submission)
- [`Client.form_br_submission()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.form_br_submission)
- [`Client.form_u4_submission()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.form_u4_submission)
- [`Client.form_u5_submission()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.form_u5_submission)
- [`Client.non_registered_fingerprint_submission()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.non_registered_fingerprint_submission)

Each of the following classes corresponds to a specific filing. They are useful for building metadata for submissions, and configuring partial update operations.

- [`CreateIndividual`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.filings.create_individual.CreateIndividual)
- [`FormBR`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.filings.form_br.FormBR)
- [`FormU4`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.filings.form_u4.FormU4)
- [`FormU5`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.filings.form_u5.FormU5)
- [`NonRegisteredFingerprint`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.filings.non_registered_fingerprint.NonRegisteredFingerprint)

## Request Lifecycle

Each time a submission request is created, the API generates a universally unique identifier (UUID) that is used to uniquely identify the submission request. This UUID is returned in the body of the `httpx.Response` and referred to as the `request_id` throughout the documentation. It can be used in subsequent requests to update, delete or retrieve the filing. The `request_id` can be extracted using [`extract_filing_request_id()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.utils.extract_filing_request_id). To retrieve the results for the request, pass the `request_id` back to the filing’s submission method as an argument.

Submission requests are processed synchronously or asynchronously depending on the filing. Synchronous submissions are processed immediately, and will return the result status immediately provided there are no server-side validation errors. The only filing that currently supports synchronous submission requests is [`CreateIndividual`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.filings.create_individual.CreateIndividual). All other submission filings are asynchronous.

For asynchronous submissions, the API will process the request in the background, as long as the submission passes the server-side validation check. The submission response will contain the `request_id`, but it does not include information on the processing itself, which must be retrieved in a subsequent request using the `request_id`. Background processing can take from 5 to 15 minutes when the [Filing Status](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/submission-api.html#filing-status) is [`FilingStatus.SUBMITTED`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.filings.base_filing.BaseFilingOps.FilingStatus.SUBMITTED). FINRA asks users to wait at least this long before requesting the result status.

If a server-side validation failure does occur, the `filing_status` will be set to `DRAFT`, if the filing supports it. Information related to the validation error can be retrieved by calling the submission method with the `request_id`. The response will contain a `result_status` field with the value `FAILED_VALIDATION`, which can be extracted using [`extract_filing_result_status()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.utils.extract_filing_result_status). The `result_status_description` field will include any error and warning messages, which can be extracted using [`extract_filing_result_status_desc()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.utils.extract_filing_result_status_desc).

Read more about the [Overall Flow](https://developer.finra.org/docs#submission_api-api_basics-overall_flow) for submission requests in the official API documentation.

## Filing Status

The request flow for a submission depends on the value of the [`FilingStatus`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.filings.base_filing.BaseFilingOps.FilingStatus), which specifies the state of a submission.

There are three available values:

- [`FilingStatus.DRAFT`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.filings.base_filing.BaseFilingOps.FilingStatus.DRAFT)
- [`FilingStatus.SUBMITTED`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.filings.base_filing.BaseFilingOps.FilingStatus.SUBMITTED)
- [`FilingStatus.VALIDATE`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.filings.base_filing.BaseFilingOps.FilingStatus.VALIDATE)

The [`FilingStatus`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.filings.base_filing.BaseFilingOps.FilingStatus) can be set on the filing object using the [`set_filing_status()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.filings.base_filing.BaseFilingOps.set_filing_status) method, if supported by the filing. The [`CreateIndividual`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.filings.create_individual.CreateIndividual) and [`NonRegisteredFingerprint`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.filings.non_registered_fingerprint.NonRegisteredFingerprint) filings only support [`FilingStatus.SUBMITTED`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.filings.base_filing.BaseFilingOps.FilingStatus.SUBMITTED), and do not allow this value to be altered.

### Submitted Filing Status

The following example builds an initial submission using [`FilingStatus.SUBMITTED`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.filings.base_filing.BaseFilingOps.FilingStatus.SUBMITTED) for a [`FormBR`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.filings.form_br.FormBR) filing. The filing is submitted to the API, and the `request_id` is extracted from the response.

```python
from finra.filings.form_br import FormBR
from finra import utils

f = FormBR()                                   # branch office registration
(
    f.set_filing_status(f.FilingStatus.SUBMITTED)  # finalize submission
     .set_filing_type(f.FilingType.INITIAL)        # initial filing
     .set_filing_data({...})                       # add some filing data
)                                                  # methods chained inline

r = c.form_br_submission(filing=f)                 # submit the filing

r.raise_for_status()

request_id = utils.extract_filing_request_id(r)    # UUID for request
```

To check the status of the submission, call the same submission method again with the `request_id` as the first argument. The `result_status` will be `PROCESSED` when it is complete. A value of `PROCESSING` indicates the API server is still working, and to wait several minutes before re-checking the status. If the `result_status` is `FAILED` or `FAILED_VALIDATION`, it means an error or warning has occurred.

```python
r = c.form_br_submission(request_id)  # check the status of the submission

r.raise_for_status()

result_status = utils.extract_filing_result_status(r)  # done if "PROCESSED"

result_status_description = \
    utils.extract_filing_result_status_desc(r)         # message / errors

data = r.json()  # submission data, wrapped with response metadata
```

### Draft Filing Status

The primary advantage of using draft submissions is that they can be updated and re-validated as many times as needed, without having to file amendments. The following example builds an initial draft submission using [`FilingStatus.DRAFT`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.filings.base_filing.BaseFilingOps.FilingStatus.DRAFT) for a [`FormBR`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.filings.form_br.FormBR) filing. It submits the draft, and extracts the `request_id` from the response.

```python
from finra.filings.form_br import FormBR
from finra import utils

f = FormBR()                                   # branch office registration
(
    f.set_filing_status(f.FilingStatus.DRAFT)  # draft submission
     .set_filing_type(f.FilingType.INITIAL)    # initial filing
     .set_filing_data({...})                   # add some filing data
)                                              # methods chained inline

r = c.form_br_submission(filing=f)             # submit the draft

r.raise_for_status()

request_id = utils.extract_filing_request_id(r)  # UUID for request
```

To retrieve the draft submission data, call the same submission method again with the `request_id` as the first argument.

```python
r = c.form_br_submission(request_id)  # use the same method to get the draft

r.raise_for_status()

data = r.json()  # draft submission data, wrapped with response metadata
```

### Validate Filing Status

A server-side completeness check can be triggered for submissions in `DRAFT` status, without changing the status to `SUBMITTED`. To trigger a completeness check, create a submission with [`FilingStatus.VALIDATE`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.filings.base_filing.BaseFilingOps.FilingStatus.VALIDATE). If a draft submission does not already exist, one will be created.

```python
from finra.filings.form_br import FormBR
from finra import utils

f = FormBR()                                    # branch office registration
(
    f.set_filing_status(f.FilingStatus.VALIDATE)  # validate submission
     .set_filing_type(f.FilingType.INITIAL)       # initial filing
     .set_filing_data({...})                      # add some filing data
)                                                 # methods chained inline

r = c.form_br_submission(filing=f)                # validate the filing

r.raise_for_status()

request_id = utils.extract_filing_request_id(r)   # UUID for request
```

To retrieve the results of the completeness check, call the same submission method again with the `request_id` as the first argument. If the completeness check is unsuccessful, the `result_status` will have the value `FAILED_VALIDATION`, and the `result_status_description` will contain additional information about errors and warnings.

```python
r = c.form_br_submission(request_id)  # check the status of the submission

r.raise_for_status()

result_status = utils.extract_filing_result_status(r) # pass or fail?

result_status_description = \
    utils.extract_filing_result_status_desc(r)        # message / errors

data = r.json()  # draft submission data, wrapped with response metadata

filing_status = utils.extract_filing_status(r)        # should be "DRAFT"
```

## Filing Type

Filing types are specific to each filing, and identify a filing procedure such as an amendment or a withdrawal. They are required for all filings except [`CreateIndividual`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.filings.create_individual.CreateIndividual).

Amendments and other filing types can be created using the full filing data, or using [Operations](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/submission-api.html#operations). In this example, an amendment is created and submitted using an operation.

```python
from finra.filings.form_br import FormBR
from finra import utils

f = FormBR()                                    # branch office registration
(
    f.set_filing_status(f.FilingStatus.SUBMITTED)  # finalize submission
     .set_filing_type(f.FilingType.AMENDMENT)      # amendment
     .add_operation(...)                           # amendment operation
)

r = c.form_br_submission(filing=f)                 # submit the amendment

r.raise_for_status()

request_id = utils.extract_filing_request_id(r)    # UUID for request
```

The one exception to this pattern is [`NonRegisteredFingerprint`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.filings.non_registered_fingerprint.NonRegisteredFingerprint), which does not support `DRAFT` status or operations. However, amendments can be submitted using the full filing data, or just the delta changes in the filing data.

## Operations

Operations are instructions for updating a filing using JSON operations. If both filing data and operations are provided in a single call, operations will be ignored.

If a filing supports operations, they can be added using the filing object’s [`add_operation()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.filings.base_filing.BaseFilingOps.add_operation) method, which takes three arguments:

1. `op` is the action in a JSON operation specified as a member of the [`Op`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.filings.base_filing.BaseFilingOps.Op) enum.
2. `path` specifies the location or traversal route within a JSON document. It is based on the [RFC 6901](https://www.rfc-editor.org/rfc/rfc6901) standard, except with arrays where an additional syntax is supported to uniquely identify an element within an array, instead of relying on array indexes.
3. `value` is placed at the `path`. For operations with [`Op.REMOVE`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.filings.base_filing.BaseFilingOps.Op.REMOVE), the `value` must be omitted or `None`.

Consider the following example filing data:

```python
{
    "individualInformation": {
        "personalInformation": {
            "individualFilingName": {
                "middleName": null,
                "lastName": "lexicon"
            }
        },
        "residentialHistory": [
            {
                "id": "5f2df182-f6d0-4504-9e18-38a8c7268b77",
                "addressStartDate": "2022-01"
            },
            {
                "id": "c970abd7-37d2-4c7e-b695-b8cb7a0b5817",
                "addressStartDate": "2022-01"
            }
        ]
    }
}
```

A `path` can be specified directly as a string, or it can be specified as an iterable representing the traversal route. The following `path` selects an array element from the example data using the syntax `[<key>:<value>]`, where the key is a label within each element, and the value uniquely identifies an element in the array:

```python
"/individualInformation/residentialHistory/[id:5f2df182-f6d0-4504-9e18-38a8c7268b77]"
```

Alternatively, the same `path` can also be specified as an iterable, and elements within an array can be identified uniquely using a (key, value) 2-tuple:

```python
["individualInformation", "residentialHistory", ("id", "5f2df182-f6d0-4504-9e18-38a8c7268b77")]
```

The following code block uses operations to modify the example filing data:

```python
from finra.filings.form_br import FormBR

f = FormBR()                                   # branch office registration
(
    f.set_filing_status(f.FilingStatus.DRAFT)  # draft submission
     .set_filing_type(f.FilingType.INITIAL)    # initial filing
     .add_operation(
         f.Op.ADD,                                          # add op
         ["individualInformation", "personalInformation"],  # path
         {"firstName": "John", "lastName": "Smith"}         # value
         )
     .add_operation(
         f.Op.REMOVE,                                       # remove op
         ["individualInformation", "residentialHistory",
          ("id", "5f2df182-f6d0-4504-9e18-38a8c7268b77")]   # path
         )                                                  # no value
)
```

Read more about operations for [Partial Updates](https://developer.finra.org/docs#submission_api-api_basics-partial_update) in the official API documentation.

## Update Draft

[Operations](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/submission-api.html#operations) are particularly useful for submissions in `DRAFT` status, which can be updated as many times as needed. To update a draft submission, provide the `request_id` as the first argument in the filing’s submission method, along with the filing object containing the update operations.

```python
from finra.filings.form_br import FormBR
from finra import utils

f = FormBR()                                   # branch office registration
(
    f.set_filing_status(f.FilingStatus.DRAFT)  # draft submission
     .set_filing_type(f.FilingType.INITIAL)    # initial filing
     .add_operation(...)                       # add operations
)

r = c.form_br_submission(request_id, filing=f)   # submit PATCH update

r.raise_for_status()
```

The default behavior for an update is to use a PATCH request, which will merge the filing data with the update data, preserving fields that are not included in the update. To replace a data sub-structure instead of merging it, use a PUT request by setting `put=True` in the filing’s submission method. Read more about the difference between PATCH and PUT requests [here](https://medium.com/@mirzasreza/understanding-the-difference-between-put-and-patch-in-restful-apis-6aa456388fe3).

The `filing_status` can also be changed in a PATCH/PUT request without providing any filing data or operations. This can be used to finalize the submission and process it to FINRA by changing the value to [`FilingStatus.SUBMITTED`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.filings.base_filing.BaseFilingOps.FilingStatus.SUBMITTED), or to trigger a completeness check on the draft filing by changing the value to [`FilingStatus.VALIDATE`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.filings.base_filing.BaseFilingOps.FilingStatus.VALIDATE).

```python
from finra.filings.form_br import FormBR
from finra import utils

f = FormBR()                                    # branch office registration
(
    f.set_filing_status(f.FilingStatus.SUBMITTED) # finalize submission
     .set_filing_type(f.FilingType.INITIAL)       # initial filing
)                                                 # no data or operations

r = c.form_br_submission(request_id, filing=f)    # submit PATCH update

r.raise_for_status()
```

## Delete Draft

Only submissions in `DRAFT` status can be deleted. To delete a submission, provide the `request_id` as the first argument in the filing’s submission method, and set `delete=True`.

```python
r = c.form_br_submission(request_id, delete=True)     # delete the draft

r.raise_for_status()
```

The status of the deletion can be tracked in a subsequent request using the `request_id`. Once the submission is deleted, the `result_status` in the response will be set to `DELETED`. Deletion is processed in the background, and may take several minutes.

```python
r = c.form_br_submission(request_id)                  # track the deletion

r.raise_for_status()

result_status = utils.extract_filing_result_status(r) # should be "DELETED"

result_status_description = \
    utils.extract_filing_result_status_desc(r)        # message / errors
```

## Client-Side Validation

Client-side validation is available through the [`Client`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.client.Client) class. This functionality **DOES NOT** currently support the [`AsyncClient`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.async_client.AsyncClient) class.

Client-side validation uses the [`Validator`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.filings.validator.Validator) class to validate filing data and metadata on the client-side before it is submitted to the API. Client-side validation is completely optional, and is not intended as a replacement for the API’s server-side validation process. However, it can be used as a supplemental tool to catch errors prior to submission.

The [`Validator`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.filings.validator.Validator) class validates a filing’s JSON object against its JSON Schema, which defines the expected structure and allowed values for the object. It is effectively a proxy for the `jsonschema.Draft7Validator` class, which can validate JSON objects against schemas that follow the [JSON Schema Draft 7](https://json-schema.org/draft-07) specification. See more information about the `jsonschema` validation process [here](https://python-jsonschema.readthedocs.io/en/stable/validate/).

During client-side validation, the schemas are fetched directly from the API and stored in memory, and are accessible from the client’s `schema_registry` attribute. This significantly reduces validation time because each schema component only needs to be fetched once. To free up resources when all validation is complete, and the schemas are no longer needed, just clear the schema registry. For more information about this design and implementation, see [ADR 0004 - Client-Side Submission Validation](https://github.com/hawkberry/finra-py/blob/main/docs/adr/0004-client-side-submission-validation.md).

To perform client-side validation within a client’s submission method, set `validate=True`. If the filing passes, it will then be submitted to the API. If it fails, a `jsonschema.ValidationError` will be raised.

```python
from finra.filings.form_br import FormBR

f = FormBR()

# ...add some filing data or operations

r = c.form_br_submission(
    filing=f,              # submit the filing
    validate=True          # validate client-side before submission
    )

c.schema_registry.clear()  # clear local store, free up memory
```

The [`Validator`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.filings.validator.Validator) class can also be used outside the client. However, it still requires a client to fetch the schemas. This can be useful to validate the filing data without submitting it to the API. The schema registry can also be managed outside the validator, which enables it to be reused to prevent redundant network operations; many schema parts are shared across filings. The validator provides two methods for determining whether a JSON object conforms to a JSON Schema: [`Validator.is_valid()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.filings.validator.Validator.is_valid) and [`Validator.validate()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.filings.validator.Validator.validate).

```python
from finra.filings.form_br import FormBR
from finra.filings.validator import Validator

schema_registry = {}  # save to reuse schemas across multiple validators

f = FormBR()

# ...add some filing data or operations

obj = f.build()       # filing data/metadata as a JSON object for submission

v = Validator(                                # create validator object
    c,                                        # client
    f.schema_url,                             # top-level schema URL
    schema_registry=schema_registry           # optional, reusable
    )

v.validate(obj)                  # raises jsonschema.ValidationError on fail

schema_registry.clear()  # cleared schemas will need to be re-fetched
```

# Getting Help

[Getting Help](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/help.html): Troubleshooting and support guidance covering diagnostic logging, bug reports, known FINRA API issues, and common `finra-py` problems.

This page describes how to troubleshoot problems, report bugs, and get assistance with `finra-py`.

## Bug Reporting

If you are experiencing a problem with the client, first ensure you’re using the most recent version. You can see the version you’re using by running `from importlib import metadata as md; print(md.version('finra-py'))` from within Python. You can also make sure you have the most recent version by executing the command `pip install --upgrade finra-py`. If you are running the most recent version, and you are still experiencing problems, the next step is to enable logging and inspect the output.

### Enable Logging

This client library performs diagnostic logging of its activity using Python’s [logging](https://docs.python.org/3/library/logging.html) module. To enable logging, add a handler to the root logger. The default output stream for [StreamHandler](https://docs.python.org/3/library/logging.handlers.html#logging.StreamHandler) is `sys.stderr`.

```python
import logging

logging.getLogger('').addHandler(logging.StreamHandler())  # write to stderr
```

Sometimes, this additional logging is enough to help you debug your application. Before asking for help, carefully review the logs and determine whether you can identify and resolve the issue yourself. You may be the best person to investigate and fix it!

You can set the log-level as appropriate. To log the HTTPX requests and responses using ordinary logging, you can set the root logger’s log-level to `DEBUG`:

```python
logging.getLogger('').setLevel(logging.DEBUG)  # set the log-level to DEBUG
```

Alternatively, if you want to only see what the client is logging, call [`base_client.get_logger()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.get_logger) to get the client’s logger and configure it directly.

However, you should be mindful about where your data is being logged. These ordinary logging configurations will not redact sensitive data in the logs. If you need log redaction, for example if you’re submitting a bug report, use [`debug.enable_bug_report_logging()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.debug.enable_bug_report_logging). See below.

### Bug Report Logging

If you still can’t figure out what’s going wrong, this library provides a special utility for preparing bug reports that collects diagnostic logs. This utility redacts sensitive values and common secrets such as tokens, API keys, CRD numbers, SSNs, DOBs, etc. If you need to provide logs in a bug report, please use this utility to generate the logs you submit, and write them to a file (see the second example below). It is not necessary to separately enable logging (as in the previous example); the bug reporting utility configures the required logging automatically.

**IMPORTANT: Log redaction is only a best effort, and is not guaranteed to be perfect. Never share your logs without verifying that all secret information has been properly redacted. It is your responsibility to ensure that your information is secure.**

The bug report utility configures dedicated loggers for the `finra-py` client, authentication, and debug modules. The logging handlers created by this utility write diagnostic logs from `finra-py` to the configured stream or file. Users may provide their own stream or file destination, but any additional logging written to that destination by external code is outside the control of this library. When filing bug reports, provide this utility a dedicated log file location so that the file contains only `finra-py` logs.

The bug report utility (and the `DEBUG` log-level in general) is not designed to be used in production code. All logged output is processed and recorded, which creates a performance penalty. Be aware that a value collision can occasionally occur during redaction, which may result in unintended fields being redacted or inaccurate redaction labels. For more information about this design and implementation, see [ADR 0005 - Diagnostic Logging and Log Redaction](https://github.com/hawkberry/finra-py/blob/main/docs/adr/0005-diagnostic-logging-redaction.md).

The recommended practice is to enable bug report logging at the beginning of your program before creating the client, so that the entire API interaction is recorded. To terminate bug report logging, exit the program.

```python
from finra.debug import enable_bug_report_logging

enable_bug_report_logging()  # enable at beginning, log to sys.stderr

# ...get a client
# ...do some requests
# ...then exit the program
```

When submitting logs as part of a bug report, write the logs to a file by passing the `filename` as the first argument. Unless explicitly turned off, the default behavior is to also write logs to `sys.stderr`. To turn this functionality off explicitly set `stream=None`. You can also write to a custom stream by passing the file-like stream object as the `stream` keyword argument.

```python
from finra.debug import enable_bug_report_logging

filename = 'my_log_file.txt'  # some log file

enable_bug_report_logging(filename=filename, stream=None) # only log to file

# ...get a client
# ...do some requests
# ...then exit the program
```

### Submit Your Ticket

You are now ready to write your bug report. Before submitting an issue, please ensure it includes the following information. Issues may be closed if they cannot be investigated effectively:

- Include code: reproducing the reported behavior requires code demonstrating the failure.
- Include logs: it is difficult to debug problems without logs.
- Redact logs: issues may be closed or deleted if logs are not adequately redacted. This is for your own protection.
- Attach log files: logs that are copy-pasted into the issue message field will not be accepted. Please write them to a file and attach it to your issue.
- Follow the issue template: this is not strict, but you should at least include all the information it asks for.

You can file an issue on the `finra-py` [Issues Page](https://github.com/hawkberry/finra-py/issues) on GitHub.

## Known FINRA API Issues

Before reporting bugs on GitHub, please make sure your issue is due to the client implementation, and not the FINRA API.

The FINRA API has a number of known behaviors and inconsistencies that may appear to be client issues. These issues have been reported to FINRA, but some may remain unresolved for an extended period of time.

The following is a list of known FINRA API issues and inconsistencies. This list is not exhaustive, and you may encounter issues that are not yet documented here. This section will be updated as known issues are resolved or new issues are discovered.

### Submission API

The Submission API has several discrepancies between the FINRA API documentation and the values defined in the JSON Schemas. Many of the examples in the Submission API are also inconsistent with the JSON Schema definitions, but those are beyond the scope of this section.

1. The API documentation for Form BR lists `WITHDRAW` or `CLOSUREWITHDRAW` as valid filing types, however the [Form BR JSON Schema](https://schemas.api.finra.org/FINRAApiPlatformBRFiling.json) definition does not allow these values (see the [Metadata Schema](https://schemas.api.finra.org/FINRAApiPlatformBRFilingMetadata.json)). The Form BR JSON Schema definition shows that only `AMENDMENT`, `CLOSURE` and `INTIAL` filing types are accepted. For now, the client library will keep these filing types implemented on [`FormBR`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.filings.form_br.FormBR) unless they are removed from the documentation.
2. The API documentation for Form U5 lists `ignoreWarnings` as a valid metadata property, however the [Form U5 JSON Schema](https://schemas.api.finra.org/FINRAApiPlatformU5Filing.json) definition does not list this as a required value and does not allow additional properties (see the [Metadata Schema](https://schemas.api.finra.org/FINRAApiPlatformU5FilingMetadata.json)). For now, the client library will keep this feature implemented on [`FormU5`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.filings.form_u5.FormU5) unless it is removed from the documentation.

### Query Production API

This section includes issues and inconsistencies for Query API production datasets.

1. The [`BaseClient.get_weekly_summary()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.get_weekly_summary) production and mock datasets, and [`BaseClient.get_weekly_summary_historic()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.get_weekly_summary_historic) production dataset, contain undocumented values in the [`WeeklySummary.TIER_IDENTIFIER`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.WeeklySummary.TIER_IDENTIFIER) partition field: `NA` and `NMS`. They also contain undocumented [`WeeklySummary.TIER_DESCRIPTION`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.WeeklySummary.TIER_DESCRIPTION) values: `Not Applicable` and `OTC` (typo?). These values are present in both [`Endpoint.PARTITIONS`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.Endpoint.PARTITIONS) and [`Endpoint.DATA`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.Endpoint.DATA), but are not in the FINRA API documentation.
2. The [`Endpoint.METADATA`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.Endpoint.METADATA) for the [`BaseClient.get_individual_registration_validation()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.get_individual_registration_validation) production and mock datasets are missing the `datasetGroup` and `datasetName` properties.
3. For production and mock datasets, [`BaseClient.get_individual_registration_validation_details()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.get_individual_registration_validation_details) returns erroneous [`Endpoint.METADATA`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.Endpoint.METADATA) that does not match the JSON Schemas for either version of this dataset.
4. The following Fixed Income production and mock datasets do not support partitions, however they return inconsistent status codes when querying [`Endpoint.PARTITIONS`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.Endpoint.PARTITIONS); the response returns `200`, but the `statusCode` field returns `500 Internal Server Error`:
   - [`BaseClient.get_agency_tba_pricing()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.get_agency_tba_pricing)
   - [`BaseClient.get_agency_cmo_pricing()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.get_agency_cmo_pricing)
   - [`BaseClient.get_agency_mbs_trading_activity()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.get_agency_mbs_trading_activity)
   - [`BaseClient.get_agency_mbs_arm_hybrid_pricing()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.get_agency_mbs_arm_hybrid_pricing)
   - [`BaseClient.get_agency_mbs_pricing()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.get_agency_mbs_pricing)
   - [`BaseClient.get_collateralized_obligations_pricing()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.get_collateralized_obligations_pricing)
   - [`BaseClient.get_daily_cmbs_pricing()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.get_daily_cmbs_pricing)
   - [`BaseClient.get_non_agency_cmo_abs_pricing()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.get_non_agency_cmo_abs_pricing)
   - [`BaseClient.get_non_agency_cmo_pricing()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.get_non_agency_cmo_pricing)
   - [`BaseClient.get_securitized_products_errata()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.get_securitized_products_errata)
   - [`BaseClient.get_securitized_products_trading_activity()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.get_securitized_products_trading_activity)
   - [`BaseClient.get_weekly_cmbs_pricing()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.get_weekly_cmbs_pricing)

### Query Mock API

This section includes issues and inconsistencies for Query API mock datasets retrieved using mock credential types. It’s possible that some of these are also found in the production datasets, but have not been enumerated in the previous section. If you discover that is the case, please file an issue on the `finra-py` [Issues Page](https://github.com/hawkberry/finra-py/issues) on GitHub so this page can be updated.

1. Some mock datasets return empty for [`Endpoint.PARTITIONS`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.Endpoint.PARTITIONS) and [`Endpoint.DATA`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.Endpoint.DATA), even when returning a `200` status code. Requests with no data should return a `204`.
2. The [`BaseClient.get_weekly_summary()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.get_weekly_summary) and [`BaseClient.get_monthly_summary()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.get_monthly_summary) production datasets contain a [`WeeklySummary.TOTAL_NOTIONAL_SUM`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.WeeklySummary.TOTAL_NOTIONAL_SUM) field in the [`Endpoint.METADATA`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.Endpoint.METADATA) and [`Endpoint.DATA`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.Endpoint.DATA) that is not present in the mock datasets.
3. The [`BaseClient.get_otc_daily_list()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.get_otc_daily_list) mock dataset returns a `404 Not Found` status code for all endpoints, and for asynchronous requests.
4. Async requests on the **first leg** for the following Fixed Income mock datasets return a `500 Internal Server Error` status code:
   - [`BaseClient.get_agency_tba_pricing()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.get_agency_tba_pricing)
   - [`BaseClient.get_agency_cmo_pricing()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.get_agency_cmo_pricing)
   - [`BaseClient.get_agency_mbs_trading_activity()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.get_agency_mbs_trading_activity)
   - [`BaseClient.get_agency_mbs_arm_hybrid_pricing()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.get_agency_mbs_arm_hybrid_pricing)
   - [`BaseClient.get_agency_mbs_pricing()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.get_agency_mbs_pricing)
   - [`BaseClient.get_collateralized_obligations_pricing()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.get_collateralized_obligations_pricing)
   - [`BaseClient.get_daily_cmbs_pricing()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.get_daily_cmbs_pricing)
   - [`BaseClient.get_non_agency_cmo_abs_pricing()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.get_non_agency_cmo_abs_pricing)
   - [`BaseClient.get_non_agency_cmo_pricing()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.get_non_agency_cmo_pricing)
   - [`BaseClient.get_securitized_products_errata()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.get_securitized_products_errata)
   - [`BaseClient.get_securitized_products_trading_activity()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.get_securitized_products_trading_activity)
   - [`BaseClient.get_weekly_cmbs_pricing()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.get_weekly_cmbs_pricing)
5. Async requests on the **first leg** for the following Firm mock datasets return asynchronously (as expected) when queried without the `firm_crd_number`, but return **synchronously** when queried with the `firm_crd_number` (single-record query):
   - [`BaseClient.get_firm_disclosures()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.get_firm_disclosures)
   - [`BaseClient.get_firm_profile()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.get_firm_profile)
   - [`BaseClient.get_firm_registration_status_history()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.get_firm_registration_status_history)
   - [`BaseClient.get_firm_registrations()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.get_firm_registrations)
6. Async requests on the **first leg** for the following Registration mock datasets return a `404 Not Found` status code:
   - [`BaseClient.get_individual_registration_validation()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.get_individual_registration_validation)
   - [`BaseClient.get_individual_registration_validation_details()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.get_individual_registration_validation_details)
7. Async requests on the **first leg** for the following TRACE Report Card mock datasets return a `403 Forbidden` status code:
   - [`BaseClient.get_trace_agency_debt_summary()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.get_trace_agency_debt_summary)
   - [`BaseClient.get_trace_treasuries_summary()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.get_trace_treasuries_summary)
   - [`BaseClient.get_trace_corporate_bonds_summary()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.get_trace_corporate_bonds_summary)
   - [`BaseClient.get_trace_securitized_products_summary()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.get_trace_securitized_products_summary)
8. Async requests on the **second leg** for **ALL** Equity (OTCMarket) mock datasets return a `403 Forbidden` status code.
9. Async requests on the **second leg** for the [`BaseClient.get_firm_registration_types()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.get_firm_registration_types) mock dataset returns a `403 Forbidden` status code.
10. The [`Endpoint.DATA`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.Endpoint.DATA) for the [`BaseClient.get_accounting()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.get_accounting) mock dataset does not filter dates correctly when `start_date` and `end_date` parameters are provided, and instead returns dates outside the queried range.
11. The [`Endpoint.DATA`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.Endpoint.DATA) for the [`BaseClient.get_branch_delta()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.get_branch_delta) and [`BaseClient.get_individual_delta()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.get_individual_delta) mock datasets do not filter dates correctly when `start_datetime` and `end_datetime` parameters are provided, and instead returns dates outside the queried range.
12. The [`BaseClient.get_composite_branch()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.get_composite_branch) mock dataset does not filter based on provided [`BaseClient.CompositeBranchSections`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.CompositeBranchSections). Instead it returns all sections, regardless of the sections filter. This is in contrast to the [`BaseClient.get_composite_individual()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.get_composite_individual) mock dataset, which has similar section filtering functionality, and behaves as expected.
13. The [`BaseClient.get_individual_pre_registration_search()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.get_individual_pre_registration_search) mock dataset returns field names that are inconsistent with the [`Endpoint.METADATA`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.Endpoint.METADATA).
14. The [`BaseClient.get_individual_registration_validation()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.get_individual_registration_validation) mock dataset returns a `404 Not Found` status code.
15. The [`BaseClient.get_registered_individual_search()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.get_registered_individual_search) mock dataset returns a `middleName` field that is not in production or mock metadata. This field cannot be used as a `fields` or `sort_fields` query parameter.
16. The [`Endpoint.DATASETS`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.Endpoint.DATASETS) for the [`BaseClient.get_broker_dealer_firm_list()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.get_broker_dealer_firm_list) mock dataset **Version 2** shows `supportedGetById` as `True`, indicating that the dataset supports single record query. This is incorrect, since **Version 2** of this dataset passes the Individual CRD Number as a query parameter, rather than accessing a URL subpath. This is also inconsistent with the value of `supportedGetById` shown for the production dataset.
17. The [`Endpoint.DATASETS`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.Endpoint.DATASETS) for the [`BaseClient.get_broker_dealer_firm_list()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.get_broker_dealer_firm_list) mock dataset shows `supportsRecordLimit` and `supportsRecordOffset` as `False`, indicating that this dataset does not support pagination. The [`Endpoint.DATA`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.Endpoint.DATA) for the mock dataset also does not accept `limit` and `offset` keywords. However, this is inconsistent with the production dataset which shows `supportsRecordLimit` and `supportsRecordOffset` as `True`. Therefore, pagination is implemented in the client’s query method.
18. The [`Endpoint.DATASETS`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.Endpoint.DATASETS) for the [`BaseClient.get_u4_form_prefill()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.get_u4_form_prefill) mock dataset shows `supportsRecordLimit` as `True` (even though `supportsRecordOffset` is `False`), indicating that this dataset supports pagination. However, this is inconsistent with the production dataset which shows `supportsRecordLimit` as `False`. Therefore, pagination is **not** implemented in the client’s query method.
19. The following Registration and TRACE Report Card mock datasets do not support partitions, however they return inconsistent status codes when querying [`Endpoint.PARTITIONS`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.Endpoint.PARTITIONS), with the response returning a `200`, but the `statusCode` field shows a `500 Internal Server Error`:
    - [`BaseClient.get_accounting()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.get_accounting)
    - [`BaseClient.get_branch_delta()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.get_branch_delta)
    - [`BaseClient.get_branch_list()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.get_branch_list)
    - [`BaseClient.get_broker_dealer_firm_list()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.get_broker_dealer_firm_list)
    - [`BaseClient.get_composite_branch()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.get_composite_branch)
    - [`BaseClient.get_composite_individual()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.get_composite_individual)
    - [`BaseClient.get_individual_delta()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.get_individual_delta)
    - [`BaseClient.get_individual_pre_registration_search_v2()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.get_individual_pre_registration_search_v2)
    - [`BaseClient.get_u4_form_prefill()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.get_u4_form_prefill)
    - [`Client.get_trace_sovereign_debt_summary()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.get_trace_sovereign_debt_summary)
    - [`BaseClient.get_trace_agency_debt_summary()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.get_trace_agency_debt_summary)
    - [`BaseClient.get_trace_treasuries_summary()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.get_trace_treasuries_summary)
    - [`BaseClient.get_trace_corporate_bonds_summary()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.get_trace_corporate_bonds_summary)
    - [`BaseClient.get_trace_securitized_products_summary()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.get_trace_securitized_products_summary)
    - [`Client.get_trace_treasuries_execution_time_difference_summary()`](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/reference.html#finra.base_client.BaseClient.get_trace_treasuries_execution_time_difference_summary)

# Security Policy for `finra-py`

## Overview

| Policy Area | Evidence |
| --- | --- |
| Supported versions and metadata | [`pyproject.toml`](https://github.com/hawkberry/finra-py/blob/main/pyproject.toml) |
| Dependency and supply-chain | [Dependabot](https://docs.github.com/code-security/dependabot); [Dependency Review](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/concepts/supply-chain-security/dependency-review); [CodeQL](https://github.com/apps/github-advanced-security) |
| Published artifacts and provenance | [PyPI Attestations](https://pypi.org/project/finra-py/#files) |
| Source inventory and file integrity | [Release SBOMs](https://github.com/hawkberry/finra-py/tree/main/.sbom) |
| License and change history | [LICENSE](https://github.com/hawkberry/finra-py/blob/main/LICENSE); [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/hawkberry/finra-py/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) |
| Application and network boundary | [ADR 0001](https://github.com/hawkberry/finra-py/blob/main/docs/adr/0001-client-architecture-http-boundary.md) |
| Authentication and token storage | [ADR 0002](https://github.com/hawkberry/finra-py/blob/main/docs/adr/0002-authentication-token-management.md); [Authentication and Client Creation](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/auth.html) |
| Client-side submission validation | [ADR 0004](https://github.com/hawkberry/finra-py/blob/main/docs/adr/0004-client-side-submission-validation.md) |
| Diagnostic logging and redaction | [ADR 0005](https://github.com/hawkberry/finra-py/blob/main/docs/adr/0005-diagnostic-logging-redaction.md); [Getting Help — Bug Reporting](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/help.html#bug-reporting) |
| Vulnerability reporting | [GitHub Private Vulnerability Reporting](https://github.com/hawkberry/finra-py/security) |

## Supported Versions

This policy applies to the latest released version of `finra-py` and its direct runtime dependencies: (1) `authlib`, (2) `httpx`, (3) `jsonschema`, and (4) `tzdata` (Windows only). Supported dependency ranges are defined by [`pyproject.toml`](https://github.com/hawkberry/finra-py/blob/main/pyproject.toml).

Security fixes are provided for the latest version only. Older releases are not currently maintained as separate security-support branches. Breaking changes, deprecations, removals, and security-related dependency changes are documented through the release and [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/hawkberry/finra-py/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md) where applicable.

## Dependency and Supply-Chain

Dependency vulnerability is monitored through GitHub’s dependency graph and [Dependabot](https://docs.github.com/code-security/dependabot) alerts. As part of the automated CI workflow, [Dependency Review](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/concepts/supply-chain-security/dependency-review) checks dependency changes introduced through pull requests, and CI audits the resolved dependency set on pushes and pull requests. A dependency security issue may result in a `finra-py` release that changes only dependency minimums when that is sufficient to exclude an affected version.

Repository security checks include GitHub [CodeQL](https://github.com/apps/github-advanced-security) and secret scanning with push protection. These controls support the `finra-py` development process but do not replace an application's own security testing or risk assessment.

## Provenance and File Integrity

Release distributions are built from tagged repository state and published to PyPI using Trusted Publishing. [PyPI Attestations](https://pypi.org/project/finra-py/#files) provide cryptographic proof of provenance through verifiable records for each published release.

Each release also includes a versioned CycloneDX JSON SBOM in the [`.sbom/` directory](https://github.com/hawkberry/finra-py/tree/main/.sbom). The SBOM provides a machine-readable inventory of source files and dependencies, with SHA-256 hashes of the source files it inventories.

## Application and Network Boundary

`finra-py` is an open-source Python client library that runs in the calling application's process. It sends requests directly to the FINRA API Platform and related resources, and returns standard `httpx.Response` object directly to the application.

Asynchronous status/result URLs and JSON schema retrieval are restricted to approved hosts over HTTPS, and embedded credentials are rejected. For JSON schema URLs, these constraints are applied to redirects. For FINRA API and related resource URLs, redirect following is disabled entirely. These restrictions reduce the risk of exposing access tokens to unintended hosts.

Optional client-side validation checks filing data against the FINRA API's published JSON Schemas before submission, but does not replace the API's server-side validation.

`finra-py` does not pass requests through a service operated by the project maintainer. `finra-py` does not remotely store application or API data, or collect telemetry, analytics, advertising, or usage data.

See [ADR 0001 — Client Architecture and HTTP Response Boundary](https://github.com/hawkberry/finra-py/blob/main/docs/adr/0001-client-architecture-http-boundary.md) and [ADR 0004 — Client-Side Submission Validation](https://github.com/hawkberry/finra-py/blob/main/docs/adr/0004-client-side-submission-validation.md).

## Authentication and Token Storage

`finra-py` uses Authlib's HTTPX integration for OAuth 2.0 authentication. API credentials are passed to the underlying OAuth2 client, and access tokens are managed by the token manager.

By default, the token manager writes token state and metadata to the file at `token_path`, which contains ordinary JSON and is not encrypted by `finra-py`. Applications can instead provide custom functions to read and write tokens using other storage systems.

See [ADR 0002 — Authentication and Token Management](https://github.com/hawkberry/finra-py/blob/main/docs/adr/0002-authentication-token-management.md) and [Authentication and Client Creation](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/auth.html).

## Sensitive Data

| Data | `finra-py` handling | Library-managed persistence |
| --- | --- | --- |
| API key and API secret | Passed to the underlying OAuth2 client | None |
| OAuth token data | Managed by the token manager | `token_path`, or application-provided callbacks |
| Request parameters and payloads | Constructed and sent by the client | None |
| API responses | Returned as `httpx.Response` objects | None |
| Asynchronous result data | Retrieved and returned by the client | None |
| JSON Schema resources | Retrieved for client-side validation | In-memory schema registry only |
| Diagnostic log data | Optional best-effort logging redaction | Depends on the configured logging output |

## Diagnostic Logging

Diagnostic logging is optional and intended for troubleshooting. The dedicated bug-report logging facility provides **best-effort** redaction for diagnostic output intended for review and sharing. Redaction is not guaranteed, so logs should be reviewed before they are shared. Response-content redaction is only applied to response content that can be decoded as JSON. Redaction is not intended for production use due to increased performance overhead.

Ordinary Python logging follows the application's logging configuration, and does not use the dedicated bug-report logging facility to redact sensitive data.

See [ADR 0005 — Diagnostic Logging and Log Redaction](https://github.com/hawkberry/finra-py/blob/main/docs/adr/0005-diagnostic-logging-redaction.md) and [Getting Help — Bug Reporting](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/help.html#bug-reporting).

## Application Responsibilities

The application remains responsible for protecting its credentials, tokens, data, and diagnostic logs, and for the security of the environment in which `finra-py` runs. These responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

- **Credentials and tokens:** Storage, access control, and encryption of API credentials and OAuth tokens, including custom token-storage functions and the systems they access. The default token file is not encrypted by `finra-py`.

- **API environment separation:** Credentials and token storage for production, Mock, and QA Test environments.

- **Response and data handling:** Processing HTTP responses, classifying application data, and controlling access, retention, and deletion of data stored, cached, backed up, or passed to other systems.

- **Diagnostic logging:** Logging configuration and destinations, and the protection of sensitive information in logs. Bug-report logging provides best-effort redaction, which does not guarantee that sensitive information is classified correctly or redacted.

- **Application security controls:** Network, endpoint, identity, access-control, monitoring, and incident-response controls for the application and its operating environment.

These responsibilities are outside the security boundary of `finra-py`.

## Reporting a Vulnerability

Please do not report suspected security vulnerabilities through a public GitHub issue. Use GitHub's [Private Vulnerability Reporting](https://github.com/hawkberry/finra-py/security) to report a suspected vulnerability. If private reporting is unavailable, use the contact address published on the [PyPI project page](https://pypi.org/project/finra-py/).

Reports are reviewed to determine validity, severity, affected versions, and appropriate remediation or disclosure steps. The expected response process is:

1. Receive and acknowledge the report
2. Assess validity and security impact
3. Determine affected versions and remediation requirements
4. Develop and test an appropriate fix
5. Release the remediation through the normal release process
6. Coordinate appropriate disclosure with the reporter

### Provide Steps and Code to Reproduce the Vulnerability

1. Describe the environment. Include the `finra-py` version, Python version, operating system, and other relevant details.
2. Describe the steps needed to reproduce the issue, the affected functionality, and relevant security impact.
3. Provide a minimal reproducible example. If possible, isolate the issue to a small, self-contained script that uses only `finra-py`.

**IMPORTANT: Do not include API credentials, OAuth tokens, token-file contents, production data, personal information, or other confidential information in a vulnerability report.** See [Bug Reporting](https://finra.hawkberry.com/en/latest/help.html) for guidance on providing error and exception logs.

### Disclosure

Please allow reasonable time for investigation and remediation before public disclosure. Confirmed security fixes are released through the normal project release process. Unless otherwise agreed to in writing, response and remediation timing depends on the nature and severity of the issue and is not a fixed service-level commitment.

# ADR 0001: Client Architecture and HTTP Response Boundary

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Decision Date:** 2026-08-09

## Context

`finra-py` provides a Python interface to the FINRA API Platform. It translates Python operations into FINRA API requests and centralizes FINRA-specific behavior, including authentication, request construction, endpoint selection (data, metadata, partitions, and datasets), field selection, filtering, sorting, pagination, server-side asynchronous requests, content-type handling, dataset-specific parameters, notifications, regulatory filings, and submission functionality. This saves applications from implementing that functionality themselves.

`finra-py` uses HTTPX for HTTP communication, a well-established Python library with support for synchronous and `asyncio`-based requests. It does not add a separate interface for standard HTTP behavior or replace HTTPX responses with `finra-py`-specific response objects or data models.

This keeps the division clear: `finra-py` handles FINRA-specific API behavior while returning standard `httpx.Response` objects directly to applications. Applications can inspect response status codes, headers, and content, and control any further processing, validation, or persistence. Higher-level features for specific FINRA API operations can still be added, provided they do not hide or replace the underlying `httpx.Response`.

## Data Flow

```text
                 Normal HTTP path
             ┌──────────────────────┐
             │ Calling application  │
             └──────────┬───────────┘
                        ▼
             ┌──────────────────────┐
             │      finra-py        │
             └──────────┬───────────┘
                        │
               access token needed?
                   ╱          ╲
                yes            no
                 │              │
                 ▼              │
      ┌─────────────────────┐   │
      │   FINRA Identity    │   │
      │   Platform (FIP)    │   │
      └──────────┬──────────┘   │             Async result retrieval (3rd leg)
                 │              │                 ┌──────────────────────┐
            access token        │                 │ Calling application  │
                 └──────┬───────┘                 └──────────┬───────────┘
                        ▼                                    ▼
             ┌──────────────────────┐             ┌──────────────────────┐
             │      finra-py        │             │      finra-py        │
             └──────────┬───────────┘             └──────────┬───────────┘
                        │                                    │
               bearer-authenticated                 pre-signed result URL
                   API request                               │
                        │                                    │
                        ▼                                    ▼
             ┌──────────────────────┐             ┌──────────────────────┐
             │  FINRA API Platform  │             │ Async Result Server  │
             └──────────┬───────────┘             └──────────┬───────────┘
                        │                                    │
                  HTTP response                        HTTP response
                        │                                    │
                        ▼                                    ▼
             ┌──────────────────────┐             ┌──────────────────────┐
             │      finra-py        │             │      finra-py        │
             └──────────┬───────────┘             └──────────┬───────────┘
                        ▼                                    ▼
             ┌──────────────────────┐             ┌──────────────────────┐
             │ Calling application  │             │ Calling application  │
             └──────────────────────┘             └──────────────────────┘
```

## Decision

**`finra-py` is FINRA-specific on the way in, and standard HTTPX on the way out.**

`finra-py` communicates directly with FINRA’s API Platform and related resources over HTTPS. It provides FINRA-specific interfaces for constructing requests and performing API operations, and returns `httpx.Response` objects directly to the calling application.

Specifically:

1. `finra-py` handles FINRA-specific authentication and request construction.
2. `finra-py` provides dedicated interfaces for the FINRA Query, Notification, and Submission APIs.
3. `finra-py` represents FINRA-specific concepts through Python interfaces, **such as**:
   a. dataset-specific methods
   b. endpoint enums
   c. field enums for selection and sorting
   d. filter objects for value comparisons, domains, and date ranges
   e. pagination parameters
   f. parameters and methods for multi-leg server-side asynchronous requests
   g. response content-type parameters
   h. other dataset-specific parameters
   i. filing objects for building regulatory submissions
   j. submission functionality for regulatory filings
4. `finra-py` does not introduce a custom response type or separate response-processing model. API requests return standard `httpx.Response` objects directly to the caller.
5. Applications control how they handle response status, headers, and content, and how they process, represent, transform, validate, or persist response data.
6. `finra-py` provides OAuth 2.0 authentication and token lifecycle management.
7. `finra-py` provides synchronous and asynchronous (`asyncio`) clients.
8. No maintainer-operated service sits between the calling application and FINRA API endpoints or related resources.
9. For server-side asynchronous check status and result requests, `finra-py` restricts URL locations to approved hosts and disables automatic redirect following, to reduce the risk of exposing access tokens to unintended hosts.

## Consequences

### Positive

- Applications do not need to implement FINRA-specific request construction themselves.
- Applications retain access to standard `httpx.Response` behavior.
- Applications are not coupled to a `finra-py`-specific response model.
- FINRA-specific functionality can be exposed through purpose-built Python interfaces without obscuring the HTTP layer.
- Applications control how responses are processed and how data is represented.
- The client has a clearly defined boundary between FINRA-specific behavior and general HTTP behavior.
- Synchronous and `asyncio`-based operation use the same underlying `finra-py` `BaseClient` class with either a synchronous or asynchronous HTTPX client.
- Asynchronous URL validation and disabled automatic redirects reduce the risk of exposing access tokens to unintended hosts.

### Negative

- Applications are responsible for processing returned responses.
- Applications must understand standard HTTP response semantics.
- Applications that require domain-specific models or additional response processing must implement those themselves.

## Alternatives Considered

### Raw HTTPX Requests

Client query methods could have applications construct FINRA API requests themselves using raw HTTPX. This would preserve the HTTP boundary, but each application would need to implement FINRA-specific behavior independently, including all of the features implemented by `finra-py` listed in the Context section above.

This was rejected because it would require applications to implement the core FINRA API functionality themselves.

### Custom Responses and Data Models

The client could convert `httpx.Response` objects into `finra-py`-specific response objects or data models.

This was rejected because it would replace the established `httpx.Response` interface with a library-specific representation and would impose assumptions about how applications should consume FINRA data. Applications should determine how returned data is represented and processed, rather than the client library.

# ADR 0002: Authentication and Token Management

- **Status:** Accepted
- **Decision Date:** 2026-08-09

## Context

`finra-py` provides a Python interface to the FINRA API Platform. To make authenticated requests, it must first obtain a valid access token from the FINRA Identity Platform for the provided credentials. It must operate for different API environments and credential types, and manage token expiration. If an application persists tokens, the application controls where and how they are stored.

The FINRA API Platform uses OAuth 2.0 for authentication and authorization. `finra-py` provides an interface for API authentication without reimplementing the OAuth 2.0 protocol or requiring an application to build and maintain its own token-management logic.

API credentials and OAuth tokens require special security considerations. Applications may already have established controls for managing secrets and storing credentials, so `finra-py` must not require a particular storage system or security model. Applications remain responsible for protecting credentials and persisted tokens, including controlling access and retention, managing encryption, and configuring diagnostic logging. The default token file is not encrypted.

`finra-py` supports synchronous and asynchronous (`asyncio`-based) authentication. Asynchronous token acquisition must use a non-blocking asynchronous HTTPX client. Applications must also be able to create and configure an asynchronous client before entering the `asyncio` event loop. Synchronous storage callbacks run inline and can block the event loop, so applications should use asynchronous callbacks for network-based storage. Authentication configuration and token state must remain separate for the production, Mock, and QA Test environments and for each credential type.

`finra-py` runs within the calling application’s process. It does not provide a maintainer-operated authentication service, route application traffic through maintainer infrastructure, or remotely store application or API data. FINRA authorization and entitlement policies are outside this decision and depend on the calling application and the FINRA API Platform.

This ADR addresses authentication and token management, not the broader HTTP client architecture established by [ADR 0001 — Client Architecture and HTTP Response Boundary](https://github.com/hawkberry/finra-py/blob/main/docs/adr/0001-client-architecture-http-boundary.md).

## Decision

`finra-py` will use Authlib’s OAuth 2.0 HTTPX integrations to handle the OAuth 2.0 protocol and `TokenManager` to manage token lifecycle and persistence. This avoids maintaining a separate OAuth 2.0 implementation. Applications control how credentials are supplied and how tokens are persisted, and can configure token access through custom callbacks. By default, tokens are stored in a local JSON file.

Specifically:

1. OAuth 2.0 authentication will use Authlib's `OAuth2Client` and `AsyncOAuth2Client` rather than a `finra-py` implementation of the OAuth 2.0 protocol.
2. API keys and secrets will be supplied to the OAuth2 session. `TokenManager` will not manage them, and the default token file will not contain them.
3. `TokenManager` will hold the raw OAuth token in memory, along with its creation timestamp and the `token_write_func` callback used to persist the updated token state.
4. Persisted token state will include `finra-py` metadata and the raw OAuth token, allowing token age and expiration to be evaluated when a client is reconstructed.
5. Applications can use `token_read_func` and `token_write_func` callbacks to customize token persistence, and use their existing storage and security controls. By default, the token is stored in a local JSON file at the application-provided `token_path`.
6. The default token writer will write an application-managed file; it will not provide application-specific encryption or act as a credential store.
7. `get_client()` and `get_async_client()` will centralize token loading and lifecycle checks. They will reuse a stored token if it meets the configured `min_expires_in` threshold, otherwise they will obtain a new token.
8. When checking whether to reuse a stored token, `get_client()` and `get_async_client()` will require at least one hour of remaining lifetime by default. Applications can change or disable this threshold.
9. Lower-level authentication functions will retain distinct responsibilities:
   a. loading an existing token from a local file will not fetch a replacement
   b. storage access functions will use the provided `token_read_func` to access an existing token without replacing it
   c. new-token functions will always obtain a new token
   d. build functions will construct clients from an already configured `TokenManager`
10. Automatic token refresh will be opt-in through `automatic_refresh=True`. When enabled, the underlying Authlib OAuth2 session will obtain a new client-credentials token when the current one expires and pass it to the `token_write_func` for persistence.
11. `Client.refresh_token()` and `AsyncClient.refresh_token()` operations will remain available regardless of whether automatic refresh is enabled. They will propagate the return value of the configured `token_write_func` callback.
12. Synchronous authentication will use `OAuth2Client`; asynchronous authentication will use `AsyncOAuth2Client`.
13. Asynchronous authentication functions will perform initial token acquisition using an asynchronous HTTPX client, rather than using a blocking synchronous client inside an asynchronous application.
14. Synchronous authentication functions will support creating asynchronous clients for applications that require the client instance before entering its `asyncio` event loop.
15. Asynchronous authentication functions will support synchronous and asynchronous `token_read_func` and `token_write_func` callbacks.
16. Synchronous callbacks used by asynchronous authentication functions run inline and block the event loop. Applications should use asynchronous callbacks for network I/O.
17. Synchronous authentication functions will only support synchronous callbacks.
18. Clients will expose token lifecycle information (`token_age`, `token_expires_at`, and `token_expires_in`) as read-only values.
19. When bug-report logging is enabled, authentication tokens will be registered with the library's diagnostic-log redaction mechanism before authentication state is logged. Redaction is a best-effort safeguard, not a replacement for application-level logging controls. See [ADR 0005 — Diagnostic Logging and Log Redaction](https://github.com/hawkberry/finra-py/blob/main/docs/adr/0005-diagnostic-logging-redaction.md).
20. Production, Mock, and QA Test Environment authentication endpoints and credentials will remain distinct. Applications are responsible for using the appropriate credentials and separate token storage for each environment.

## Data Flow

The authentication and refresh paths are shown together to make the relationship between token acquisition, `TokenManager`, Authlib, and the calling application explicit.

```text
              Initial Authentication
             ┌──────────────────────┐
             │ Calling application  │
             └──────────┬───────────┘
                        ▼
             ┌──────────────────────┐
             │      finra-py        │
             │    auth functions    │
             └──────────┬───────────┘                   Token Refresh
                        │                         ┌──────────────────────┐
                 existing token?                  │   Client / OAuth2    │
                 ╱              ╲                 │       session        │
              yes                no               └──────────┬───────────┘
               │                  │                          │ refresh
               ▼                  ▼                          ▼
      ┌─────────────┐   ┌──────────────────┐      ┌──────────────────────┐
      │   token     │   │  FINRA Identity  │      │    FINRA Identity    │
      │   storage   │   │  Platform        │      │    Platform          │
      └────────┬────┘   └─────────┬────────┘      └──────────┬───────────┘
               └────────┬─────────┘ new token                │ new token
                        ▼                                    ▼
             ┌──────────────────────┐             ┌──────────────────────┐
             │    TokenManager      │             │     TokenManager     │
             └──────────┬───────────┘             └──────────┬───────────┘
                        ▼                                    ▼
             ┌──────────────────────┐             ┌──────────────────────┐
             │  Authlib OAuth2      │             │ token_write_func     │
             │  HTTPX integration   │             │ application-managed  │
             └──────────┬───────────┘             │ storage or file      │
                        │                         └──────────┬───────────┘
                        ▼                                    ▼
             ┌──────────────────────┐             ┌──────────────────────┐
             │        Client        │             │        Client        │
             └──────────────────────┘             └──────────────────────┘
```

The same architectural boundary is used by synchronous and asynchronous clients. The asynchronous path uses Authlib's `AsyncOAuth2Client` for token acquisition and can await asynchronous callbacks where provided.

## Consequences

### Positive

- Applications do not need to implement the OAuth 2.0 token acquisition flow themselves.
- Authlib handles OAuth 2.0 protocol operations, reducing the amount of custom authentication code `finra-py` must maintain.
- API credentials are separated from persisted token state; the default token representation does not contain the API secret.
- Applications can use the default local token file for straightforward deployments without having to implement token serialization themselves.
- Enterprise applications can integrate token persistence with existing credential-management infrastructure through callbacks without introducing a `finra-py`-specific storage service.
- The authentication boundary remains inside the application's process, with no maintainer-operated service or authentication proxy between the application and the FINRA API Platform or related resources.
